issue.title: BUG: Filter/transform fail in some cases when multi-grouping with a datetime-like key

repository.name: pandas
repository.description: Flexible and powerful data analysis / manipulation library for Python, providing labeled data structures similar to R data.frame objects, statistical functions, and much more

issue.body: Fixes GH #10114, and a related problem in transform which was already present in 0.16.0

body:
In the meantime, here's a workaround:

``` python
simple = pd.DataFrame({
        'A': pd.Series([pd.to_datetime('2015-01-01')]), 
        'B': pd.Series([1], dtype=np.float64),
        'C': pd.Series([3], dtype=np.float64)})
simple.set_index(['A', 'B'])[simple.groupby(['A', 'B']).apply(lambda x: True)].reset_index()
```

Note: This code drops index. If you need to retain the index, do reset_index before and set_index after to retain index.

issue.title: pandas 0.16.2 groupby and transform does not properly work with datetime objects

repository.name: pandas
repository.description: Flexible and powerful data analysis / manipulation library for Python, providing labeled data structures similar to R data.frame objects, statistical functions, and much more

issue.body:
In the 0.16.2 version, transform returns original values, while in the 0.15.2 version it properly transforms the values into group counts.  The problem seems to be with how pandas deal with datetime objects.  

The only difference is the pandas version, and everything else is the same.

---

```
import pandas as pd
import datetime
df = pd.DataFrame([[pd.to_datetime(datetime.date(2015,8,10)), 'A', 10],
                   [pd.to_datetime(datetime.date(2015,8,10)), 'A', 20],
                   [pd.to_datetime(datetime.date(2015,8,11)), 'B', 30],
                   [pd.to_datetime(datetime.date(2015,8,10)), 'B', 40],
                  ], columns=['timestamp', 'name', 'value'])
grp = df.groupby(['timestamp', 'name'])['value']
grp.transform(lambda x: x.count())

```

1    2
2    1
3    1
Name: value, dtype: int64

---
## 0.16.2 version

0    10

issue.title: DataFrameGroupBy.filter returns empty dataframe when grouping by multiple columns and one column is type datetime64[ns]

repository.name: pandas
repository.description: Flexible and powerful data analysis / manipulation library for Python, providing labeled data structures similar to R data.frame objects, statistical functions, and much more

issue.body:
There seems to be a bug in the `filter` method when grouping by multiple columns, where one of the grouping columns has type `datetime64[ns]`. Here is an example:

``` python
data = [
    ('a', pd.Timestamp('2015-08-01'), 0),
    ('a', pd.Timestamp('2015-08-01'), 0),
    ('a', pd.Timestamp('2015-08-02'), 1),
    ('b', pd.Timestamp('2015-08-01'), 2),
    ('b', pd.Timestamp('2015-08-02'), 3),
    ('c', pd.Timestamp('2015-08-01'), 4),
    ('c', pd.Timestamp('2015-08-02'), 5),
    ('c', pd.Timestamp('2015-08-02'), 5),
]
data = pd.DataFrame(data, columns=('A', 'B', 'group_number'))
groups = data.groupby(['A', 'B'])
assert len(groups) == 6  # OK

filtered = groups.filter(lambda x: len(x) > 1)
assert len(filtered) == 4  # AssertionError
```

Now, if I change the timestamps to strings, `filter` works as expected:

``` python
data2 = data.copy()
data2['B'] = data2['B'].astype(str)
groups2 = data2.groupby(['A', 'B'])
filtered2 = groups2.filter(lambda x: len(x) > 1)
assert len(filtered2) == 4  # OK
```

Also, `filter` works as expected when grouping by _only_ column B, regardless of whether it contains timestamps or strings.

What's going on here? Am I missing something or is this actually a bug? Thanks!
